thomas.note: The lamp image is part of this saying, which begins with another image.
Thomas 39 ends with serpents and doves; its preceding keys and entry saying is a separate comparison.
The saying about two leaders is followed by images of wine and a patch.
Thomas omits the question about offering to remove the speck.

title: Trees and their fruit

thomas.note: A related image of a tree and its fruit; the saying makes a different comparison.
The fruit and treasure images are also found in Luke 6:44–45.

note: Matthew 12:33 is a separate occurrence of the tree and fruit image.

title: The wedding guests and the bridegroom

thomas.note: Thomas also speaks of fasting after the groom leaves; the setting and wording differ.

title: The return of the unclean spirit
The householder’s new and old treasures
The camel and the needle’s eye
speaker: Jesus

title: The doorkeeper
note: Mark’s doorkeeper and Luke’s watchful servants are related images, but the scenes differ.

title: Physician, heal yourself
note: Luke uses the Greek word parabolē here; it is often translated ‘proverb’.

thomas.note: A related but different proverb: a doctor does not heal those who know them. The preceding prophet saying is closer to Luke 4:24.
A parallel to the first-and-last saying in Luke 13:30, not to the closed-door scene.

title: What is holy and the dogs
speaker: Jesus

thomas.note: The images of holy things, dogs, pearls and pigs recur; Thomas ends in a damaged passage.

title: The measure used
speaker: Jesus
note: The sayings use a common image of measuring, in different settings.

thomas.note: The easy yoke and rest recur with different wording.
Thomas speaks briefly about anxiety over clothing; the Gospel passages develop additional images.
Thomas speaks of seeking and finding in a different dialogue.
Seeking and finding, and knocking and opening, recur; the latter clause is reconstructed in brackets.
The reed and fine clothing recur; Thomas has damaged wording and a different ending.

title: The shepherd struck and the sheep scattered
speaker: Jesus quotes Scripture
note: Both accounts quote Zechariah 13:7.

title: Lips and heart
speaker: Jesus quotes Isaiah
note: Matthew and Mark record Jesus quoting Isaiah 29:13.

title: Good news and release
speaker: Jesus reads Isaiah
note: Luke records Jesus reading from Isaiah in the synagogue.

title: Remember Lot’s wife
speaker: Jesus
note: Jesus recalls Lot’s wife in a discourse about the coming day.

thomas.note: The second part speaks of enduring treasure safe from destructive creatures; the first part is a pearl story.

title: A city on a hill
speaker: Jesus
note: Matthew 5:15 also appears in the lamp on a stand.

thomas.note: Both say that a city on a height cannot be hidden; Thomas adds that it cannot fall.
Thomas speaks of light within a person. The light image is thematic; the sayings differ.

title: The narrow and wide gates
speaker: Jesus
note: Luke 13:24 is already included with the closed door; its setting and emphasis differ.

thomas.note: The foxes and birds contrast with the Son of Humanity having nowhere to rest; Thomas is partly reconstructed.
The harvest and few workers recur; the surrounding settings differ.

title: Fishers of people
speaker: Jesus
note: The calling of fishers differs from the fish-selection story in Thomas 8.

title: The yeast of the Pharisees
speaker: Jesus
note: These warnings use yeast differently from the kingdom leaven comparison.

thomas.note: Thomas speaks of a grapevine planted outside the Father; the wording and application differ.

title: The inside and outside of the cup
speaker: Jesus

thomas.note: Thomas asks about the maker of the inside and outside; the Gospel criticisms and applications differ.

title: Tombs and hidden graves
speaker: Jesus
note: Matthew compares outwardly beautiful tombs with hidden uncleanness; Luke speaks of unmarked graves.

title: Faith and the mountain
speaker: Jesus
note: Luke speaks of a mulberry tree; the conditions and settings differ among the sayings. Matthew 17:20 has textual variation in some witnesses.

thomas.note: Thomas connects the mountain moving with two people making peace in a house.
Thomas joins making two into one with a mountain moving; the conditions and framing differ.

title: Keys and the barred entrance
speaker: Jesus
note: Luke names a key of knowledge; Matthew describes the kingdom being shut. The hosted World English Bible numbers the Matthew saying as verse 14; other editions number it as verse 13.

thomas.note: The keys and blocked entry are followed by a separate serpents-and-doves saying.
The dog preventing cattle from eating shares the theme of hindering others; it is a different comparison.

title: Green and dry wood
speaker: Jesus
note: The saying is given on the way to the crucifixion; its application is not spelled out here.

title: Hidden and revealed
speaker: Jesus

thomas.note: Thomas combines what is hidden being revealed with a call to know what is before one.
The hidden and revealed saying follows a discussion of conduct, fasting, prayer and food.

note: Matthew and Luke also include a related instruction about speaking openly; Mark 4 and Luke 8 place the hidden saying beside a lamp image.

thomas.note: Both sayings speak of fire cast on the world or earth; the wording and setting differ.

title: The kingdom and its coming
speaker: Jesus
note: Translations differ on whether Luke says the kingdom is within or among those addressed.

thomas.note: Thomas speaks of the kingdom within and outside; the sayings and their contexts differ.
Thomas says the kingdom is spread over the earth but unseen; the wording differs from Luke.

title: Reading the sky and the present
speaker: Jesus
note: Matthew 16:2b–3 is absent in some early manuscripts.

thomas.note: Thomas compares reading the sky and earth with failing to recognize the present; the surrounding exchange differs.
The hand saying follows a statement about mysteries in Thomas; Matthew places it in teaching about giving.
Thomas contrasts lending at interest with giving without expecting return; the emphasis differs.

title: Division within a household
speaker: Jesus
note: These sayings about division differ from the divided kingdom and strong man passage.

thomas.note: Thomas also speaks of division within a house; its concluding wording differs.

title: John and the least in the kingdom
speaker: Jesus

thomas.note: Thomas uses a little-child formulation in its comparison with John; the wording differs.

title: Hearing and keeping the word
speaker: Jesus and a woman in Luke 11; Jesus in Luke 23
note: Luke 23:29 occurs in a different setting from the exchange in Luke 11.

thomas.note: Thomas combines a woman’s blessing and a reply about hearing with a saying about childlessness; Luke places these in different settings.

title: Testimony about destroying the temple
speaker: Witnesses report words attributed to Jesus
note: Witnesses report a claim attributed to Jesus at his trial; the reports differ from John 2:19–21.

thomas.note: Thomas attributes destroying a house to Jesus; its ending is damaged and it does not mention three days.

title: The threshing floor and chaff
speaker: John the Baptist
note: John the Baptist speaks of gathering grain and burning chaff.

title: The house and the den of robbers
speaker: Jesus quotes Scripture
note: Jesus quotes Scripture in the temple; the quoted language is also used in 2 Clement 14:1.

title: Serpents and offspring of vipers
speaker: Jesus
note: This figurative address appears in a warning to scribes and Pharisees.

title: Peter, the rock and the keys
speaker: Jesus
note: The keys given to Peter differ from the barred entrance and key of knowledge in Matthew 23 and Luke 11.

title: The disciple and the teacher
speaker: Jesus
note: Luke gives the disciple and teacher comparison; Matthew also speaks of a servant and lord.

title: The coming like lightning
speaker: Jesus
note: The lightning comparisons have different settings and wording in Matthew and Luke.

title: Guests from east and west
speaker: Jesus
note: Both sayings mention a gathering with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; Luke places it in a different exchange about the closed door.

title: The lost sheep of Israel
speaker: Jesus
note: These sayings use the image of lost sheep for the house of Israel; they are distinct from the story of the one lost sheep.
